Lola Young has announced the Everything Begins Tour, a 17-date North American headline run set for spring 2027. It will be her first full tour of the region since she stepped away from live work in 2025, after a period in which her return happened gradually through individual performances and festivals rather than another long itinerary. The new run follows a year spent rebuilding her live schedule without immediately replacing the tour she had cancelled.

The break began after she collapsed during her set at All Things Go in New York and then cancelled her remaining performances for the foreseeable future. She said she needed time to work on herself and asked listeners to give her "a second chance" when she was ready to return. There was no comeback date attached to that message. Among the cancellations was the North American tour built around *I'm Only F**king Myself*, so the break stopped a full regional run before it could happen. When performances resumed, they came one at a time rather than as a replacement for the cancelled tour.

At the Grammys, "Messy" won Best Pop Solo Performance, and she performed the song during one of her first appearances after the break. Headline shows in Britain and festival sets followed through the year, including a return to All Things Go. Those dates expanded her live schedule without immediately turning into another long tour. By the time the new run was announced, she had already spent months performing regularly again.

[apple:song:6768357139:6768357142]

"From Down Here" arrived during that rebuilding period, giving the new shows material written after the break. She has said inspiration hit the day after the Grammys and that she went into the studio with James Blake to make the song. She described it as coming from the uneasy position of missing an old high while knowing that a more grounded life is safer and more rewarding. The track is calmer than much of *I'm Only F**king Myself*, but the writing remains direct rather than softening the tension at the center of the song.

The tour name, "Everything Begins," reverses the wording of Young's "Everything Ends" tattoo. By the time it was announced, she had already returned to individual stages, released new music and spent months performing without committing to another long itinerary. The 17-date run is the first time since the cancellations that her return to the region has been built around a full headline tour rather than isolated appearances, restoring the kind of schedule that disappeared when she stepped away from touring.
